pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #17
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What does a crotchet look like? (1 mark)
   A. A dot only
   B. A zigzag
   C. A filled-in oval with a stem
   D. An empty circle

2. On the Kenyan flag, white stands for (1 mark)
   A. the people
   B. peace and honesty
   C. blood
   D. the sky

3. When the anthem is sung, you should (1 mark)
   A. run
   B. stand straight and be quiet
   C. sit and talk
   D. play

4. Repeating a small group of notes in a rhythm helps listeners to (1 mark)
   A. change the words
   B. stop listening
   C. remember the pattern
   D. forget the pattern

5. What does pivoting mean? (1 mark)
   A. Turning on the landing foot without moving it
   B. Jumping over the ball
   C. Running quickly
   D. Dropping the ball

6. The giraffe stretch mainly improves (1 mark)
   A. smell
   B. hearing
   C. flexibility
   D. only speed

7. The top part of the recorder is the (1 mark)
   A. bell
   B. head joint
   C. foot joint
   D. middle joint

8. Why should the knees lift high when sprinting? (1 mark)
   A. To give a stronger, longer stride
   B. To slow down
   C. To look funny
   D. To trip others

9. What sound do you hear if a hole is not fully covered? (1 mark)
   A. A drum sound
   B. Nothing at all
   C. A clear note
   D. A squeak or weak sound

10. In a supine float, you lie (1 mark)
   A. on your back with ears in the water
   B. curled up
   C. standing
   D. face down

11. What is the minimum distance a defender must keep from the player with the ball? (1 mark)
   A. 5 metres
   B. 1 centimetre
   C. 10 metres
   D. 0.9 metres

12. How long does a quaver rest last? (1 mark)
   A. Two beats
   B. Half a beat
   C. Four beats
   D. One beat

13. What is the theme of the montage in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Ball games
   B. Food
   C. Weather
   D. Wild animals

14. Which player mainly tries to stop the shooter? (1 mark)
   A. WA
   B. GK
   C. GS
   D. C

15. Which is a non-melodic percussion instrument? (1 mark)
   A. Thumb piano
   B. Shaker
   C. Marimba
   D. Xylophone

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Explain how to compose a short melody using d, r and m. (4 marks)

17. Explain how animal games help to keep the body healthy. (4 marks)

18. Explain why a pair of quavers is the same length as one crotchet. (3 marks)

19. Name any two players' positions in netball. (2 marks)

20. What is the difference between a working portfolio and a display portfolio? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #17 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — A filled-in oval with a stem
   A crotchet has a filled note head and a stem.

2. B — peace and honesty
   White stands for peace and honesty.

3. B — stand straight and be quiet
   Show respect.

4. C — remember the pattern
   Repetition gives shape and makes the rhythm easier to remember.

5. A — Turning on the landing foot without moving it
   A player keeps one foot down and turns on it.

6. C — flexibility
   Stretching increases flexibility.

7. B — head joint
   The head joint has the mouthpiece.

8. A — To give a stronger, longer stride
   High knees produce a powerful stride.

9. D — A squeak or weak sound
   Leaks make squeaks.

10. A — on your back with ears in the water
   You look at the sky.

11. D — 0.9 metres
   A defender must stand at least 0.9 metres away.

12. B — Half a beat
   A quaver rest is half a beat of silence.

13. A — Ball games
   The montage is themed ball games.

14. B — GK
   The Goal Keeper guards the goal and defends against the shooter.

15. B — Shaker
   A shaker gives a rattling sound but not different notes for a tune.

SECTION B
----
16. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a rhythm. Give a syllable to each note. Use steps. End on d as a crotchet. Sing it and show the hand signs. Write the syllables under the rhythm names.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

17. (4 marks)
   Answer: They strengthen muscles, stretch the body, improve balance and coordination and make the heart and lungs stronger.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: A quaver is half a beat. Half plus half makes one whole beat. A crotchet is one beat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

19. (2 marks)
   Answer: Goal Shooter, Goal Attack, Wing Attack, Centre, Wing Defence, Goal Defence, Goal Keeper. Any two.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each position.

20. (2 marks)
   Answer: A working portfolio holds work in progress. A display portfolio holds the best finished works for showing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
